title: SQL Guard
summary: Warns before running SQL that touches every row or drops data, like UPDATE/DELETE without WHERE, and asks for the table name first.
description: SQL box with a small tokenizer (comments and strings ignored) that flags UPDATE/DELETE without WHERE, a commented-out WHERE, always-true conditions, DROP and TRUNCATE, asks before writes on production, shows estimated rows and requires typing the table name.
catches: UPDATE or DELETE with no top-level WHERE
A WHERE that is only inside a -- or /* */ comment, with a one-tap uncomment
Simple always-true conditions after WHERE or OR (1=1, TRUE, id = id, 'a'='a')
Any write when env is in productionEnvs
Estimated affected rows from your estimateRows
limits: Pattern checks only: it does not parse full SQL or prevent SQL injection, and a query with a WHERE can still be destructive
Tokenizer understands -- and /* */ comments, '…' and $$…$$ strings, and "…", `…` and […] identifiers; MySQL # comments are not recognised
"WHERE 1=1 AND …" (a query-builder pattern) is flagged as always-true even though AND narrows it
Not dialect-aware beyond that; CTEs are judged by their writing verb
a11y: Visible <label>; Cmd/Ctrl+Enter runs; hints in a polite live region via aria-describedby
Confirmation is a labelled group; focus moves into it, Escape closes
Type-the-table input has a <label>; Enter runs only when it matches
Environment shown as text with a colour dot
server: Run with least-privilege credentials, prefer transactions and read-only connections, and enforce production write approval on the server.
stops: Helps catch a DELETE without WHERE before it runs
